REQUIRED safety hook (COORD-476): blocks manual git merge/cherry-pick/push of the CONFIGURED integration branches (coord/project.config.js integrationBranch per repo + the coord workspace base) — not a hardcoded literal. Fail-closed: helper crash or unresolvable config is a nonzero exit, which blocks.

Runtime authority barrier for shell (COORD-645, WIRING REPAIRED COORD-663). WIRING: bare `node …`, so the harness's own PreToolUse envelope reaches fd 0 UNCHANGED. It must stay that way. The shipped wiring was `printf '%s' "$TOOL_INPUT" | node …`; TOOL_INPUT is unset in this harness, so the pipe REPLACED the real envelope with an empty string, `decide()` saw no command and no write target, and the barrier returned allow("no_write_target") on EVERY call — inert for its whole life while reading like a check that passed (COORD-480). Never reintroduce a `printf`/`echo`/`cat`/`$TOOL_INPUT` prefix or any other stdin producer: reconstructing the payload from the environment is how this control was severed. PAYLOAD ABSENCE IS A REFUSAL, NOT A PERMIT (COORD-663, the COORD-635/642/656/626/660 class): with a lock active and no payload obtainable, the hook exits 2 with `payload_unavailable` rather than waving the call through. ENFORCED while ANY governed lock is active: denies permanent deletion and destructive Git; denies any shell command that names a CANONICAL governance path as a write target (redirect / tee / sed -i), parsed with a quote-aware lexer so neither `> "quoted/path"` nor a `>` inside an argument is misread. NO command is exempt — including coord/scripts/gov: gov performs its canonical mutations in-process, transactionally, under lock and journaled, and never by shell redirect, so scanning it costs nothing, while an exemption keyed on a gov invocation appearing somewhere in a compound command was itself a bypass (COORD-645-F1). With NO active lock the barrier deliberately does not engage (bootstrap/adoption/read-only stay unblocked). NOT ENFORCED: writes made INSIDE a program the shell launches (a script, `node -e`, an editor) are invisible to a PreToolUse hook — only the command text is inspected.

Runtime authority barrier for file writes (COORD-645, WIRING REPAIRED COORD-663). WIRING: bare `node …`, so the harness's own PreToolUse envelope reaches fd 0 UNCHANGED — no `printf`, no `echo`, no `$TOOL_INPUT` reconstruction, ever (see the Bash matcher above for the full account of how that prefix made this barrier inert). PAYLOAD ABSENCE IS A REFUSAL, NOT A PERMIT (COORD-663): with a lock active and no payload obtainable the hook exits 2 with `payload_unavailable`. WHAT IS ENFORCED, while ANY governed lock is active: (1) every Write/Edit/MultiEdit/apply_patch that lands in the CANONICAL tree is refused — uncommitted canonical changes get swept into whatever the lock holder commits next, which is the 2026-08-04 false-authorship incident — with symlinks, `..` traversal and case aliases resolved before classifying, and WITHOUT consulting actor identity, so an unresolvable or forged actor gains nothing; (2) an actor the trusted owner-lease registry POSITIVELY DISOWNS is refused inside a ticket worktree too; (3) worktree confinement is preserved — a session acting inside one worktree may not write outside it. TRUST MODEL: every GRANT derives from trusted runtime state (the lock/identity files only gov writes, under lock and journaled) and from the filesystem read through realpath. The tool payload and the process environment are actor-controlled — the agent exports its own COORD_SESSION_ID/COORD_PROVIDER — so self-asserted identity may only ADD refusals and can never widen authority. With NO active lock the barrier does not engage. NOT ENFORCED — IN-WORKTREE OWNERSHIP (COORD-645-F2; accepted limitation by human-admin scope decision, tracked by COORD-648): a write INSIDE an active ticket worktree by an actor whose identity cannot be resolved is PERMITTED. Treat this as an unenforced surface, never as a check that passed. A PreToolUse hook has no trustworthy authentication channel — the harness gives every sub-agent of a conversation the same session id, hides the per-sub-agent COORD_SESSION_ID override from hooks, and every other visible signal is shared or actor-settable — so there is nothing to enforce with, and denying would deny the legitimate owner's own work.
